model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the performance of several methods measured against an increasing number of edited records. The x-axis is labeled "Number of edited records" and operates on a logarithmic scale with major vertical grid lines and tick labels at $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$; data is plotted at four discrete points starting prior to $10^1$ and concluding past $10^3$. The y-axis is partially obscured but appears to be labeled "Success Rate (%)", utilizing a linear scale that ranges from 0 to over 100, marked by horizontal grid lines at intervals of 20. The graph contains six distinct solid lines, four of which correspond to entries in the legend. The green line, labeled "ROME" with square markers, starts highest at approximately 45, exhibits a steep upward trend to 96 at the third data point, and extends beyond the upper limit of the y-axis before the final x-axis value. An unlabeled brown line utilizing diamond markers begins near 28, rises to 59 by the third point, and finishes at roughly 73. The purple line labeled "MEMIT," featuring circular markers, starts at roughly 26, ascends to 46 by the second data point, and concludes at 61. The red line for "IKE" uses upward-pointing triangles, showing a relatively steady climb from an initial value of 20 to a final value of 47. The blue line, representing "FT" with downward-pointing triangles, begins around 8, increases to 35 by the third point, and ends at 42. Lastly, an unlabeled black line with circular markers starts lowest at approximately 2, rises to 28 by the third point, and levels out almost completely to end at 29.
